claims.text: Adding machine-learning-enhanced atomistic descriptors to composition–property models will significantly improve predictions of phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
Ab initio simulations can provide quantitative atomistic or structural descriptors for high-entropy alloys.
The proposed descriptors quantitatively capture local lattice distortions, bond-length fluctuations, and configurational entropy.
CrMnFeCoNi is a multielement HEA that can have disordered solid-solution structures.
HEAs such as equimolar CrMnFeCoNi exhibit pronounced local chemical disorder or heterogeneity.
HEAs such as equimolar CrMnFeCoNi exhibit pronounced local lattice distortions.
The framework is applicable at elevated temperatures relevant to thermal insulation.
The framework's advantage is limited to HEAs in which local lattice distortion and chemical heterogeneity dominate phonon scattering.
The framework may not provide an advantage for nearly ordered alloys or when other heat-transfer mechanisms are significant.
Local lattice distortions and variations in bond-length distributions mediate phonon scattering.
Local distortions and bonding fluctuations dictate phonon scattering in the targeted HEAs.
Representing atomic-scale disorder allows the model to account for deviations from composition-averaged properties and thereby reduce prediction error.
The proposed framework will reduce prediction error by approximately 30–50% relative to models using only averaged structural descriptors.
Current phonon-thermal-conductivity models for HEAs rely on averaged properties, neglect atomic-scale effects, and consequently show significant discrepancies from experiment.
The estimated 30–50% improvement is based on trends in predictions of other HEA properties.
The amount of prediction improvement may vary with the extent of local disorder and thermal conditions.
Failure to achieve at least a 30% error reduction relative to conventional models across the tested compositions and conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
